title: JSON attest output is prefixed by human license text
evidence: Attest calls enforce_license_policy, whose successful branches print colored text to stdout at lines 162 and 178, before JSON or SCITT serialization.
trigger: Run attest --format json or --format scitt with an active license or evaluation quota.
impact: stdout is not parseable as the advertised JSON document.

title: Sidecar blocks all requests on a single idle client
evidence: The serial incoming loop calls blocking stream.read with no timeout and no worker dispatch.
trigger: A permitted same-UID client connects without sending bytes.
impact: All subsequent status, verify and attest requests wait indefinitely.

title: Sidecar skips license enforcement on event writes
evidence: Authorized POST /attest directly calls ledger::append_event; inspected ledger.rs:120-169 contains no license check, unlike CLI Attest.
trigger: An authenticated sidecar client appends events with an expired or exhausted license.
impact: The CLI license halt is bypassed through the sidecar endpoint.

title: Unknown obligations silently become successful empty verification
evidence: verify_statement_content drops unknown obligation strings in the wildcard arm. omega0.rs:142-144 returns true when obligations is empty.
trigger: Call verify_statement_content with valid modality and only an unknown or misspelled obligation such as reproduciblity.
impact: The Python-facing verification API returns true after removing the requested constraint instead of rejecting unsupported obligations.

title: Contradiction verification ignores kernel nogoods
evidence: The method calls omega0::verify(&js), which constructs an empty nogoods set at omega0.rs:133-134; Contradiction merely checks absence from that set at lines 152-154. contradict_knowledge updates self.atms at bindings.rs:112-119 but this verification method never queries it.
trigger: Assert a contradiction for content X, then call verify_statement_content(X, epistemic, [contradiction]).
impact: The API returns true for an obligation that the same kernel state marks contradicted. This is a verification-result defect, not a proven execution-gate bypass.

title: Preserve a statement when removing a sole docstring
evidence: visit_Expr returns None for every constant expression (16-18); transmute_file writes ast.unparse directly back to the source (80-87), with no repair for empty suites.
trigger: Prune a valid function or class whose only statement is a docstring, for example def f(): followed by its sole indented string literal.
impact: The transformed function/class has an empty body; its written source cannot be parsed/imported. Existing tests contain other statements and do not cover this case.

title: Recognize imported bindings before suppressing required imports
evidence: _find_import_flags checks ast.alias.name but ignores asname, then visit_Module suppresses importing os/signal when those module names appeared (60-75). Injected handlers always reference bare os and signal (26-35).
trigger: Prune a module using import os as operating_system or import signal as sig and a broad exception handler.
impact: The injected handler raises NameError at its first missing bare binding instead of performing its intended fail-stop action.

title: REPL spins indefinitely after stdin reaches EOF
evidence: read_line result is checked only with is_err(); Ok(0) falls through to eval_line of an empty buffer and immediately repeats the loop. CLI declares Repl in main.rs:56.
trigger: Close stdin with Ctrl-D or run the interactive REPL with an exhausted pipe.
impact: Process remains running, repeatedly prints prompts and consumes CPU/output resources.

title: Sexagesimal addition overflows for accepted u64 operands
evidence: User inputs are parsed as unrestricted u64 at lines 53-56; f1 + f2 and s1 + s2 + carry use unchecked arithmetic at 58 and 61.
trigger: sexa add 18446744073709551615 0 1 0, or two maximal fraction operands.
impact: Debug builds panic; release builds can wrap and report an incorrect exact Q60 result.

title: Public projection continues when mandatory secret scanner is unavailable
evidence: Lines 84-93 warn and continue when command -v gitleaks fails. The same script reaches git push at line 145 after the separate biometric gate; the header claims a mandatory zero-finding secret scan.
trigger: Run a non-dry public projection on a machine without gitleaks; other file/size and authorization checks pass.
impact: The publication consumer can push an unscanned tree. Biometrics approves publication but does not inspect secrets; no actual secret or leak was observed.

title: Dry-run force-moves the existing release branch
evidence: git commit-tree and git branch -f release/v5.0-clean execute at lines 103-104 before the DRY_RUN exit at lines 127-132.
trigger: Invoke --dry-run while release/v5.0-clean points to a previous prepared release and earlier checks pass.
impact: A validation run replaces an existing release ref and creates a commit, potentially discarding the intended release tip from that branch. No script was run.

title: Delete only proven orphan WAL files
evidence: Lines 178–189 delete every *.db-wal and *.db-shm without checking an open database, checkpoint, or base file. CANONICAL_PROTECTED_DIRS is never consulted. main calls purge_anergy with destructive mode by default.
trigger: Run the CLI on a workspace containing a live WAL-mode SQLite database or a closed database with uncheckpointed committed WAL data.
impact: Committed transactions can be discarded; live connections can continue against unlinked WAL/shared-memory files.

title: Scope listener resets to an explicitly selected operation
evidence: purge_anergy(workspace_path) opens Path.home()/.gemini/antigravity/conversation_summaries.db and updates every RUNNING/not_fully_idle record at lines 203–206. This is independent of workspace_path.
trigger: Run an ordinary non-dry workspace cleanup while another chat is active.
impact: Unrelated running chats are marked idle outside the selected workspace.

title: Zero-weight agents still veto pooled hypotheses
evidence: Weights default missing entries to zero (78), but p <= 0 vetoes the hypothesis before checking the weight (80-82).
trigger: Pool opinions with a zero-weight or omitted-weight agent assigning zero to a hypothesis supported by positive-weight agents.
impact: An excluded agent changes or zeros the result, violating weighted geometric pooling semantics.

title: Bootstrap stores unencrypted private key in encrypted-key column
evidence: generate_identity serializes PKCS8 with NoEncryption at lines 29-33; bootstrap_genesis inserts priv_pem directly into private_key_enc at lines 63-65.
trigger: A caller invokes bootstrap_genesis on an empty ledger.
impact: The resulting database and its backups contain the signing private key in plaintext; access to the database permits key recovery. No active bootstrap caller was located in the targeted package search.

title: Provenance ATTESTED accepts caller-supplied receipt labels without verifying evidence
evidence: verify_integrity only checks startswith("b3:") for receipt/export/anchor digests; effective_provenance_level promotes presence to verified levels. evaluate_provenance_claim runtime scope checks non-null runtime/receipt and derivation, then returns ATTESTED at lines 438 onward.
trigger: A caller constructs an EXECUTION_RECEIPT envelope with execution_runtime set and execution_receipt_digest_b3="b3:" and evaluates a RUNTIME_EXECUTION claim.
impact: The exported arbiter API can attest execution without any receipt verification or content binding. Repository search found tests and package export, no protected runtime consumer; this is an arbiter correctness flaw, not a demonstrated deployment authorization bypass.

title: Additional LSP headers are consumed as JSON payload bytes
evidence: After Content-Length, the parser reads exactly one line as an assumed empty delimiter (47-49), then consumes content_length bytes immediately (52-53).
trigger: An incoming message places a Content-Type header after Content-Length, followed by the actual empty line and JSON body.
impact: The extra header consumes the delimiter read and the remaining delimiter is included in the body; JSON parsing fails and stream framing is desynchronized.

title: Daemon installer reports success exit after launchctl rejection
evidence: Non-success output.status prints an error at 218–223 but function returns Ok at 225.
trigger: launchctl load runs successfully as a process but returns a nonzero exit status.
impact: Install command exits successfully although service activation failed; automation cannot reliably detect the failure.

title: Seqlock stress oracle accepts mixed finite snapshots and even zero successful reads
evidence: Reader accepts every snapshot whose kinetic_energy and enstrophy are not NaN; all writer values at lines 406-414 are finite. It does not compare fields to epoch_id. RetryExhausted increments a counter; final assertion at 439 checks only total_torn == 0 and ignores _total_valid/_total_exhausted.
trigger: The example reads fields from different publications, reads initial zero state before the writer, or exhausts every read.
impact: The example can print coherence validated at 100% despite never establishing a coherent publication. This is a defect in the example validation, not evidence of an actual production torn read.

title: Demo presents simulated authentication and print-only fail-stop as actual guarantees
evidence: USER supplies the asserted operator at lines 99–100, signature/key are fixed MOCK byte strings at lines 105–106, effect is a hardcoded result at line 113, and fail-stop only prints at line 179. Line 189 claims the demo proves Human Gate, Cryptographic Provenance and Fail-Stop.
trigger: Run or present this demonstration as its documented 13-step hardware authorization demonstration.
impact: Viewers receive success/ATTESTED/kernel-transition claims without a biometric call, actual signature, dispatch gate or kernel-state transition. This is an example/evidence defect, not an asserted production bypass.

title: Concurrent installer mutations are never followed by an integrity audit
evidence: audit_target_integrities runs before the 10-thread injection phase. After concurrent injections the final success condition checks only return codes and never audits resulting files.
trigger: Parallel installer runs all return zero but leave duplicated, broken, or inconsistent targets.
impact: The stress demo still prints its final idempotency and safety conclusion, leaving concurrency corruption undetected.

title: Repeated consensus hash replaces a prior epoch
evidence: state_hash is UNIQUE and insertion uses INSERT OR REPLACE; hash construction excludes epoch.
trigger: Persist the same consensus state at two different epochs, including a stable one-validator simulation.
impact: SQLite replacement removes the previous epoch row, so ledger history silently loses observations.

title: Compute the actual repository root in setup
evidence: SCRIPT_DIR is scripts/c5_setup, and a single dirname sets REPO_ROOT to scripts. Consequently line 24 looks for scripts/.agents rather than repository .agents, then skips copying and prints success at line 42.
trigger: Run the setup script at its committed location.
impact: The advertised governance/skill installation silently fails.

title: Stub exporter labels tautologies as verification of extracted claims
evidence: generate_lean_code discards statement semantics: every extracted axiom becomes forall x, True (74), every theorem becomes True := by trivial (80–81). process_file injects this under Verificación Formal / Puente Isomorfo (107).
trigger: Run exporter on a document containing a nontrivial or false theorem.
impact: Generated Lean proves only True while the injected section presents a formal bridge to the document claim. No evidence of a production authorization consumer is asserted.

title: Concurrent publish calls can expose mixed attestation fields
evidence: publish(&self) increments seq without writer exclusion. Writer A takes seq 0->1; writer B takes 1->2, allowing read() to observe an even sequence while both publishers write payload. Fields are public and the type has no single-writer capability. Module is exported at src/lib.rs:114.
trigger: Two threads call the public safe publish method on the same shared contract.
impact: read() may return a count and hash from different publications despite the documented atomic snapshot guarantee. No active production call site established.

title: Remove await from the synchronous onStart example or declare it async
evidence: The fenced example declares onStart() { and then uses await this.mcp.registerServer(...).
trigger: A reader copies the MCP reconnection example into a TypeScript class.
impact: The example fails to parse because await occurs in a non-async method.

title: Sample-peak scaling is presented as a true-peak guarantee
evidence: Formula uses max(abs(x)) of discrete samples (453) then guarantees zero inter-sample saturation (454).
trigger: Implement the prescribed scalar ceiling on a waveform whose reconstructed inter-sample peak exceeds its sample peak.
impact: Samples meet the ceiling while reconstructed output can exceed it; documented -1dBTP guarantee requires oversampled/reconstruction peak measurement.

title: Password breach checker reports success when its API request fails
evidence: The example uses curl -s without checking its status or HTTP response, then treats any absent grep match as OK at lines 45-51.
trigger: DNS/TLS/network failure or an HTTP error body instead of the expected range response.
impact: A failed verification is presented as a password with no recorded breach matches. This finding concerns the documented executable example only.

title: Group creation wizard completes without creating a group
evidence: createGroup only logs participants (lines 5-8); no Baileys import, connection, or group-create call exists. The command invokes it unconditionally for nonempty arguments at line 15.
trigger: Invoke the advertised self-contained group wizard with participant arguments.
impact: The script exits successfully after displaying a creation message while producing no WhatsApp group.
